news.headline: Fed Hikes Rates for First Time in 3 Years — US 10Y Near 5%
news.what_happened: The US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates last week for the first time in three years, driving the US 10-year Treasury yield to 4.998% (+1.03% on the day). Markets absorbed the news — Nasdaq +0.40%, S&P +0.17% — but the Dow lagged at -0.18%. The rate hike reflects the Fed's response to sticky US inflation.
news.why_it_matters: A Fed rate hike + US 10Y at 5% is a global tightening signal. It risks triggering FII outflows from EMs including India. Rate-sensitive Indian sectors — banks, NBFCs, real estate — face near-term valuation headwinds. However, FII was still net buyer Friday (+₹599.50 Cr), suggesting the hike was largely anticipated.

news.headline: Crude Oil WTI Falls to $94.07/bbl (-2.09%); Brent -1.77% to $97.53
news.what_happened: WTI crude fell to $94.07/bbl (-2.09%) and Brent to $97.53/bbl (-1.77%). Context: WTI had been above $100 on Sep 18 before correcting sharply. Natural gas also fell -1.31%. The energy complex is in a clear downtrend this week despite prior supply concerns.
news.why_it_matters: Crude is the dominant input cost driver across multiple Indian sectors: jet fuel for airlines (35-40% OPEX), synthetic rubber and carbon black for tyre makers (60-70% input cost), crude derivatives for paint companies (40-50% raw materials). A sustained crude decline from $100+ is a major multi-quarter tailwind for margins across these sectors.

news.headline: FII Net Buyers +₹599.50 Cr; DII Net Buyers +₹1,019.70 Cr (Friday Sep 18)
news.what_happened: Both institutional categories were net buyers on Friday. FIIs bought ₹599.50 Cr net in the cash segment; DIIs (LIC + mutual funds) added ₹1,019.70 Cr. Combined institutional buying of over ₹1,619 Cr despite the Fed rate hike and rising US yields.
news.why_it_matters: Continued institutional buying is a strong bullish signal. DII support cushions any FII volatility. Combined buying suggests domestic confidence in India's growth story despite global tightening.

news.headline: GIFT Nifty at 23,361 — Flat Open Signalled
news.what_happened: GIFT Nifty (SGX Nifty equivalent) is trading at 23,361, essentially flat vs Nifty 50 prev close of 23,346. Intraday range: 23,287.5 – 23,393.5.
news.why_it_matters: A flat GIFT Nifty signals a cautious open. No gap-up or gap-down expected. This means stocks will trade near their Friday closing prices, making our watch zones around prev close highly relevant. Do not adjust entry levels upward at open.

news.headline: India Exports Aug 2026: +26.1% YoY to $43.8bn; Trade Deficit Narrows
news.what_happened: India's merchandise exports in August 2026 grew 26.1% YoY to $43.8 billion. The trade deficit narrowed. Forex reserves at $780.78 billion (fell $4.92bn in the week to Sep 11). Direct tax collections up +13% YoY.
news.why_it_matters: Strong export growth and a narrowing trade deficit are structurally positive for INR and India's current account. This supports the case for sustained FII inflows over the medium term.

news.headline: Xi Jinping US State Visit Thursday — Geopolitical Wildcard This Week
news.what_happened: Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled for a US state visit on Thursday this week. Global Flash PMIs (US, EU, UK, Japan) are due mid-week. China markets are closed today (Mid-Autumn Festival).
news.why_it_matters: Xi-US meeting could be a significant risk event for markets mid-week — either a trade war de-escalation (positive for metals, risk-on) or renewed tensions (risk-off). China markets reopen tomorrow; watch for catch-up moves in metals and the Hang Seng.
